messages:
Ava (PM): Quick sync request 1: three big asks: strict data residency, low-latency APAC SLA, and a migration path for existing tenants. Need to pick priorities for next two quarters.
Priya (Arch): High-level: we can cover spectrum: policy-first routing (declarative templates) + a placement admission controller. Which customers are pushing hardest?
Marcos (Sales): Customer A (EU finance) demands no egress from eu-west. Customer B (APAC marketplace) wants 95th <= 50ms across APAC. Customer C wants gradual opt-in with a dry-run migration.
Rafi (Eng): Engineering constraints: strict residency requires capacity reservations or node labeling with hard constraints. That affects utilization heavily. We should quantify percent util loss for 10/25/50% reserved capacity.
Liam (SRE): Operational constraints: hard pins reduce failover flexibility. Need documented fallback choreography and a regional evacuation playbook. Also need a capacity-pressure alarm that triggers cross-tenant degradation policies.
Ava (PM): Proposal: Q2 = policy templates + placement simulator + contract/security checklist. Q3 = reservation mechanism + admission controller + pilot migrations. Does that feel reasonable?
Priya (Arch): I like staged delivery. For Q2 deliverables: 1) policy template catalog (residency-first, latency-first, cost-first), 2) simulator that projects capacity and cost per template, 3) telemetry spec.
Rafi (Eng): For simulator: we'll reuse the traffic-replay infra and add a placement model. Prototype ETA: 4 weeks. Reservation mechanism complexity: two approaches1) soft tokens (preferred nodes) 2) hard allocations (dedicated slices). Recommend soft tokens for Q3 pilot.
Marcos (Sales): Soft tokens sound safer to sell initially. We'll avoid promising hard allocations until legal/procurement approves pricing model.
Zoe (Legal): If we market 2-residency-first2 templates, we must include explicit statements about fallback behavior in the contract. We can't promise absolute no-egress unless we're doing hard allocations and attested controls (KMS in region, audit logs).
Liam (SRE): Canary & ops acceptance: 72h canary with traffic ramp, <5 P0/P1 incidents. Backup route must exist to paired-region with documented latency delta and data-access implications.
Priya (Arch): Telemetry checklist: per-tenant region served histogram, prefix cache miss ratio by region, model-variant fallback counts, reservation utilization, placement-rejection rate. These drive launch gating.
Ava (PM): Launch criteria (Q2 pilot): 1) Simulator accuracy within 10% on capacity projection, 2) policy DSL + templates merged in repo, 3) dashboard panels for telemetry, 4) two pilot tenants signed.
Rafi (Eng): API sketch for policy: ```route_policy { tenant: "T123" template: "residency-first" prefer_nodes: ["eu-*"] reservation_mode: "soft" }``` We'll add a dry-run flag that returns placement outcomes without committing.
Marcos (Sales): I'll schedule pilot customers and avoid embedding hard-residency verbiage in initial contracts. Zoe, I'll share proposed pilot terms for review.
Zoe (Legal): Please include fallback SLA language and an opt-out for emergency cross-region failover. Also require customers to opt into GA only after compliance checklist passes.
Liam (SRE): Ops tooling: admission controller must expose a simulation endpoint and a mitigation plan when capacity is insufficient (e.g., degrade to latency-first, or spike autoscale).
Priya (Arch): Model compatibility note: ensure model binaries/quantization parity across regions or include explicit model-fallback rules (prefer same-variant, else degrade with rollback telemetry).
Ava (PM): Cost guardrails: define cost delta thresholds per template (e.g., residency-first <= +25% w/ options to pass cost to tenant). Need finance/pricing input.
Marcos (Sales): I'll draft a pricing appendix with options: (A) pass-through instance premium, (B) monthly reservation fee, (C) hybrid credit model.
Rafi (Eng): Dev plan: sprint 11) DSL + dry-run API, sprint 21) simulator + metrics emission, sprint 31) admission controller + pilot support. Need 2 engineers + 0.5 PM FTE.
Priya (Arch): Also propose a policy-compiler that can output capacity impact estimates and recommended placement constraints. Long-term (post-Q3): enable quotas/reservations in control plane.
Liam (SRE): Add chaos tests: scheduled regional blackout while pilot is active to validate fallback sequence and SLO impact. Runbook drill 1 week before GA.
Ava (PM): Actions: Rafi 1 draft API + dry-run spike (due in 1 week). Priya 1 policy templates + telemetry spec (1 week). Liam 1 ops runbook + chaos plan (2 weeks). Marcos 1 pilot signups + pricing sketch (1 week). Zoe 1 review pilot contract language (3 days).
ops-bot: Reminder: add roadmap PR link to #release-war-room by EOD Tue.
Marcos (Sales): On it.
Rafi (Eng): I'll push a short spike doc to the channel today with simulator assumptions.
Priya (Arch): I'll attach template examples to the PR when ready.
Ava (PM): Thanks all. We'll reconvene after spikes to lock quarter commitments.
